hero.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to full ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
hero.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire, according to a joint statement released by the United States, Israel, and Lebanon following U.S.-mediated talks at the State Department in Washington DC. The agreement requires Hezbollah to halt attacks completely and evacuate all its operatives from areas south of the Litani River.

The joint statement emphasized that both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The statement also called for the Lebanese army to take full control of security zones that would be established within Lebanon, though specifics on how these zones would be created remain unclear.

The ceasefire represents the latest attempt to stabilize a volatile situation. Israel and Lebanon previously agreed to a truce last month, but fighting has continued since that announcement. Israeli strikes have killed more than 800 people in Lebanon following the earlier agreement, while Hezbollah has continued targeting Israeli troops in southern Lebanon and launching rockets toward northern Israel.

Recent military escalation has been severe. Israel has attacked three hospitals in southern Lebanon within one week, killing nine people and wounding more than 150 according to Lebanon's health ministry. Israeli troops have also advanced deeper into southern Lebanon than they have in approximately 25 years, raising their flag over the ancient Beaufort Castle over the weekend. In response, Hezbollah launched deeper rocket attacks into northern Israel.

A significant challenge to implementation remains uncertain. Hezbollah, which operates as a semi-autonomous armed force within Lebanon, is not directly participating in the negotiations and has firmly rejected the talks. The organization has stated it will not comply with any agreements resulting from the Israel-Lebanon discussions. While the Lebanese government has accepted the ceasefire terms, Hezbollah's willingness to accept the withdrawal requirement south of the Litani River is unclear.

The two sides agreed to reconvene for additional talks beginning June 22 to work toward a comprehensive peace and security agreement. The timing reflects the fragile nature of the current arrangement.

The agreement comes as the U.S. pursues broader diplomatic efforts in the Middle East. President Trump has indicated he wants to keep Lebanon separate from Iran peace negotiations, describing them as "a very different kind of thing." Iranian officials have warned that any attack on Beirut would trigger a wider resumption of conflict in the Middle East.

The conditional nature of the ceasefire leaves open the possibility that fighting could resume if Hezbollah rejects the terms or if either side fails to implement them as outlined. Implementation success will likely determine whether this agreement achieves lasting stability or becomes another temporary pause in the conflict.

cards.headline: House Votes to Halt Iran War in Rebuke to Trump
cards.teaser: Four Republicans joined Democrats to pass a measure ending US involvement in the conflict after three previous failures.
cards.body:
The House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution on Wednesday with a 215-208 vote, requiring President Trump to seek congressional approval before continuing military operations in Iran or withdraw U.S. forces. Four Republicans crossed party lines to join Democrats: Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan. The measure succeeded after failing in three previous attempts.

The vote delivered a significant rebuke to Trump, who has downplayed the conflict's importance to the United States. This contrasts sharply with his earlier predictions that the war would result in quick and decisive victory.

cards.headline: Trump strips job protections from 8,000 federal workers
cards.teaser: President Trump signed an order moving approximately 8,000 federal positions to a new employment category that removes civil service protections.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order reclassifying about 8,000 senior federal positions into Schedule Policy and Schedule Career categories. These workers, who earn up to nearly $200,000 annually and are deemed to be "influencing" government policy, lose their civil service job protections under the change.

The reclassification converts these positions to at-will employment, allowing the administration to dismiss workers without the due process protections previously guaranteed to career civil servants. The move expands the administration's ability to reshape the federal workforce.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets share price at $135 for largest IPO in history
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's rocket company will debut on the Nasdaq next week at a valuation that exceeds Saudi Aramco's 2019 offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX set its initial public offering price at $135 per share, valuing the company at $1.75 trillion to $1.77 trillion. The offering will raise $75 billion to $85 billion, making it the largest IPO ever and surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut in both valuation and capital raised.

The space exploration company plans to list on the Nasdaq next week. Elon Musk's rocket maker announced the target price earlier than market observers expected. The capital raise reflects SpaceX's growing financing needs as it expands operations.

cards.headline: Trump to Impose Tariffs on Dozens of Countries Over Forced Labor Claims
cards.teaser: The administration proposed new tariffs on 60 economies citing trade practices involving forced labor.
cards.body:
President Trump has announced tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trading partners, including the UK, EU, Canada, Taiwan and Australia. The administration cited forced labor concerns as justification for the duties.

This represents Trump's latest attempt to revive his tariff agenda after the US Supreme Court struck down many of his previous tariffs in February. The EU has already objected, stating the move contradicts a tariff agreement reached between the US and Europe in July of last year.

cards.headline: Possible flesh-eating screwworm infection found in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA reports a possible case of flesh-eating screwworm in South Texas, which would mark the first time the parasite has crossed the US-Mexico border if confirmed.
cards.body:
The United States Department of Agriculture announced the detection of a possible flesh-eating screwworm infection in South Texas. If laboratory tests confirm the infection, it would represent the first time the invasive fly species has breached the border between the United States and Mexico.

Screwworms are parasitic fly larvae that feed on living tissue of warm-blooded animals, including humans and livestock. The species was previously eradicated from the United States through a sustained control program, making any reintroduction a serious agricultural and public health concern.

cards.headline: Ohio State reaches $100 million settlement in sex abuse cases
cards.teaser: Ohio State University's Board of Trustees approved a final $100 million settlement with survivors of sexual abuse by former team doctor Richard Strauss.
cards.body:
The Ohio State University Board of Trustees approved a $100 million final settlement with survivors of sexual abuse by Richard Strauss, a former university doctor. The settlement ends a years-long lawsuit involving multiple victims who came forward with allegations against Strauss.

The $100 million agreement represents the conclusion of legal proceedings that spanned several years. Strauss worked as a team doctor at the university, where he abused students over an extended period. The settlement provides compensation to survivors who filed claims against the institution.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon Renew Ceasefire Agreement
cards.teaser: A US-brokered deal calls for Hezbollah to stop all attacks, though a previous ceasefire was largely ignored.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire, contingent on Hezbollah ending its attacks. The US-brokered deal requires a complete cessation of fire from the Iranian-backed militia operating in southern Lebanon. The US State Department stated that both countries reject any attempt by state or non-state actors to undermine Lebanon's future.

Israel has continued military operations in southern Lebanon following the agreement, though it has refrained from striking Beirut since the deal was announced. A previous ceasefire between the parties was largely ignored, raising concerns about whether this renewed agreement will be sustained.

cards.headline: Fire at New Delhi Hotel Kills at Least 21
cards.teaser: Dozens more were injured in what appears to be the deadliest fire in India's capital in at least four years.
cards.body:
A fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people, according to authorities. Dozens more were injured in the blaze.

The fire appears to be the deadliest in the Indian capital in at least four years. Authorities did not immediately disclose the cause of the fire or the name of the affected hotel.

cards.headline: Albania Freezes Assets in Kushner Resort Investigation
cards.teaser: Protests have grown over a Sazan Island development project linked to Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump.
cards.body:
Albania froze assets connected to a resort project on Sazan Island linked to Jared Kushner. The move came as protests grew over the development, with demonstrators describing their opposition as a flamingo revolution.

The investigation involves a resort project associated with Kushner and Ivanka Trump. Albanian authorities have not disclosed the specific reasons for freezing the assets or the scope of their probe.

cards.headline: Trump Intervenes in Brazilian Politics Ahead of Election
cards.teaser: The president appears ready to support a right-wing ally in Latin America's biggest test for the left this year.
cards.body:
President Trump is intervening in Brazilian politics ahead of a crucial election that will test the strength of Latin America's political left. Trump appears ready to lend support to a new right-wing ally in the country.

The election will be the biggest test for Latin America's left this year. Trump's involvement mirrors previous instances of American presidents attempting to influence political outcomes in the region, though the specific form of his support was not detailed.

cards.headline: Phone Call Between Trump and Netanyahu Complicates Iran Talks
cards.teaser: Israel's prime minister laughed off reports of friction but has tested the patience of other US presidents.
cards.body:
A phone call between President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was described as complicating ongoing talks with Iran. Netanyahu dismissed reports of friction between the two leaders.

The House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution directing Trump to end hostilities with Iran in a 215-208 vote, with four Republicans joining Democrats. Though the measure represents a rare bipartisan rebuke, it is largely symbolic and faces an uncertain path in the Senate, where it would likely encounter a presidential veto.

hero.headline: House votes to halt Iran military operations in rebuke to Trump
hero.body:
The U.S. House of Representatives voted 215 to 208 to pass a war powers resolution directing President Trump to end military hostilities with Iran. Four Republicans joined Democrats to approve the measure, which had failed in three previous attempts. The vote marks a rare bipartisan rebuke of the ongoing military conflict.

The resolution is largely symbolic. Democrats have been unable to pass similar legislation in the Senate, where Republican support would be needed. Even if the measure cleared both chambers of Congress, Trump would likely veto it. War powers resolutions require congressional authorization for sustained military action, but presidents have historically resisted such constraints on their role as commander in chief.

The vote reflects growing unease among some Republicans about the scope and duration of military engagement with Iran. The four Republicans who crossed party lines to support the resolution represent a shift in GOP sentiment on the conflict, though the vast majority of the party remains aligned with the administration's approach. Democrats have repeatedly sought to limit Trump's authority to conduct military operations against Iran without explicit congressional approval.

The measure comes after months of escalating tensions and military action between the United States and Iran. Congressional Democrats have argued that the president exceeded his constitutional authority by ordering sustained military operations without a formal declaration of war or explicit authorization from Congress. The administration has maintained that existing authorizations and the president's constitutional powers justify the military response.

The House vote sets up a potential showdown over war powers and executive authority, even as the practical impact of the resolution remains limited. Without Senate passage and the ability to override a presidential veto, the measure serves primarily as a statement of congressional opposition to the current military posture toward Iran.

cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah stopping its attacks. The U.S. State Department issued a statement saying both countries reject any attempt by state or non-state actors to hold Lebanon's future hostage.

Following the ceasefire announcement, Israel has continued its military campaign in southern Lebanon but has not struck Beirut. The partial truce appears to be holding as both sides navigate the initial phase of the agreement.

cards.headline: California governor's race remains undecided as votes continue to be counted
cards.teaser: California's primary election for governor has not been decided, with several candidates competing to finish in the top two positions.
cards.body:
California's gubernatorial primary is deadlocked with nearly 60% of votes counted. Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News host, holds a narrow lead, followed by Democrat Xavier Becerra, the former health secretary. Billionaire environmental activist Tom Steyer trails in third place.

The state's vote-counting process is moving slowly and could take days or weeks to complete. California's primary system advances the top two finishers to the general election regardless of party affiliation, meaning a Democrat will almost certainly become the next governor of the state.

cards.headline: New ovarian cancer drug extends survival and improves quality of life
cards.teaser: A breakthrough drug for ovarian cancer is offering patients extended survival time and improved daily functioning.
cards.body:
Women treated with a new ovarian cancer drug report significantly improved quality of life and extended survival compared to previous treatments. Patients taking the medication told the BBC the drug has given them their lives back, allowing them to resume normal activities and spend more time with family.

The treatment represents a significant advancement in ovarian cancer care, a disease that has historically had limited therapeutic options. The drug's ability to both prolong life and maintain quality of life marks a departure from treatments that may extend survival but leave patients debilitated by side effects.

cards.headline: Scientists advance toward new hair loss treatments for women
cards.teaser: Researchers are making progress on developing new treatments for hair loss that could benefit women experiencing the condition.
cards.body:
Hair loss treatments for women could soon improve as scientists move closer to developing new options. BBC News examines what these breakthroughs could mean for women experiencing hair loss, highlighting the personal impact of advancing research in this field.

The progress represents a significant development for those affected by hair loss conditions, offering hope for better therapeutic solutions in the coming years.

hero.headline: SpaceX sets share price at $135 for largest IPO in history
hero.teaser: Elon Musk's rocket company will debut on the Nasdaq next week at a valuation that exceeds Saudi Aramco's 2019 offering.
hero.body:
SpaceX set its initial public offering price at $135 per share, valuing the company at $1.75 trillion to $1.77 trillion. The offering will raise $75 billion to $85 billion, making it the largest IPO ever and surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut in both valuation and capital raised.

The space exploration company plans to list on the Nasdaq next week. Elon Musk's rocket maker announced the target price earlier than market observers expected. The capital raise reflects SpaceX's growing financing needs as it expands operations.

cards.headline: Alphabet raises $85 billion for Google's AI business
cards.teaser: The tech giant's stock sale sets a record and leaves Wall Street in unprecedented territory.
cards.body:
Alphabet completed its largest-ever equity fundraising with an $80-85 billion stock sale to fund Google's artificial intelligence infrastructure investments. The offering marks the largest equity raise on record, surpassing the combined value of the three biggest IPOs ever. Berkshire Hathaway participated with a $10 billion share purchase.

The massive capital raise signals strong investor appetite for AI-related opportunities and reflects the tech industry's substantial infrastructure spending demands. Analysts noted the fundraising puts Wall Street in unprecedented territory given its historic scale.

cards.headline: Trump administration expands tariffs to 59 countries over forced labor
cards.teaser: The White House plans levies of up to 12.5 percent on nations that fail to crack down on goods made with forced labor.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has announced plans to impose tariffs between 10 and 12.5 percent on 60 trading partners, including the UK, EU, Canada, Taiwan and Australia. Officials justify the levies by citing failures to adequately address forced labor in goods production.

The move follows the Supreme Court's February decision striking down many of Trump's previous tariffs. By shifting to a forced labor rationale, the administration is employing what it describes as a more legally sustainable framework. The EU has already protested, stating the tariffs breach the spirit of a tariff agreement reached in July. Critics argue the forced labor focus serves as a pretext for protectionist trade policies.

cards.headline: Broadcom shares fall despite record earnings and revenue
cards.teaser: The chipmaker's stock dropped after its AI chip sales forecast and software revenue disappointed investors.
cards.body:
Broadcom reported record quarterly earnings and revenue, but its stock declined in after-hours trading. The sell-off was driven by disappointing guidance on AI chip sales and weaker-than-expected software revenue figures.

Investors had anticipated more aggressive growth projections for the company's artificial intelligence and semiconductor divisions. The unchanged AI chip forecast for the year fell short of market expectations, suggesting the strong results had already been factored into the stock price.

cards.headline: Trump administration contests court order on tariff refunds
cards.teaser: Officials have begun repaying some tariff money but may make it harder for certain businesses to claim full amounts owed.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is fighting a court order requiring it to refund certain tariffs. The government has started repaying some of the money to businesses but has signaled it may complicate the process for companies seeking full reimbursement.

Officials indicated they could impose additional requirements or restrictions on businesses attempting to claim tariff refunds. The legal dispute centers on tariffs that courts determined were improperly imposed. The administration's response suggests it intends to limit the financial impact of the court ruling.

cards.headline: Lab-grown diamonds increase pressure on natural gem miners
cards.teaser: The rising popularity of synthetic diamonds is creating challenges for those who search for stones underground.
cards.body:
The growing market for lab-grown diamonds is putting pressure on people and companies that mine natural gems. The synthetic diamond industry has expanded as manufacturing technology improves and consumer acceptance grows.

Natural diamond miners face increased competition from laboratory-produced alternatives that can be made at lower cost. One miner described the traditional search for diamonds by saying it requires divine fortune to discover a valuable stone. The shift in consumer preferences and market dynamics is reshaping the diamond industry.

cards.headline: Uber releases annual list of items left in vehicles
cards.teaser: The ride-hailing company's lost and found report includes dentures, butterflies, breast milk, and a dishwasher among unusual discoveries.
cards.body:
Uber has published its annual Lost & Found Index, showcasing the unusual items passengers have abandoned in the rideshare company's vehicles. The list ranges from butterflies to breast milk, highlighting the diverse range of belongings left behind in backseats across the country.

The report also identifies America's most forgetful city and reveals which day of the year sees the highest number of lost items, offering insights into passenger behavior and travel patterns throughout the year.

hero.headline: NASA declares Mars orbiter MAVEN mission over after months of silence
hero.body:
NASA has officially ended the MAVEN mission after the spacecraft lost contact with Earth following an orbital anomaly. The orbiter, which has studied Mars for more than a decade, stopped communicating with ground stations over a weekend and has not resumed contact despite extensive recovery efforts.

MAVEN, which stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution, launched in 2013 and reached Mars orbit in 2014. According to NASA, all subsystems were working normally before the spacecraft passed behind Mars. When it reappeared on the other side of the planet, the spacecraft had stopped transmitting data back to Earth.

"Telemetry showed all subsystems working normally before it orbited behind Mars," NASA said in a statement. "The spacecraft and operations teams are investigating the anomaly to address the situation."

Throughout its operational life, MAVEN studied the upper Martian atmosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. The research helped scientists understand a fundamental question about Mars: why the planet lost most of its atmosphere over billions of years. Scientists determined that the sun itself was responsible, as solar wind gradually stripped away much of the planet's air. This atmospheric loss transformed Mars from a potentially wet and warm world capable of supporting life into the cold and dry planet it is today.

Beyond its primary research mission, MAVEN served an important secondary role as a communications relay for NASA's two Mars rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance. The spacecraft transmitted data from these surface rovers back to Earth, supporting their ongoing exploration and scientific discoveries.

The loss of MAVEN leaves NASA with fewer active orbiters around Mars. However, the space agency still maintains two other spacecraft in Mars orbit: the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in 2005, and Mars Odyssey, launched in 2001. Both continue to operate and study the planet.

Mission operators expressed the emotional impact of losing the long-lived spacecraft. The loss was compared to losing a loved one, reflecting the deep connections that develop between teams and the spacecraft they operate over many years of continuous work.

Despite the end of active operations, MAVEN's contributions to science will continue to benefit researchers. The extensive data collected by the orbiter throughout its years of operation will inform scientific understanding of Mars and planetary atmospheres for years to come. NASA has not announced immediate plans for a replacement mission with similar atmospheric research objectives focused on studying the Martian upper atmosphere and its interaction with solar wind.

cards.headline: Google ordered to add clearer source links in AI search, allow UK publisher opt-outs
cards.teaser: Google must modify its AI Overviews feature to provide clearer attribution and let UK publishers opt out of having their content used.
cards.body:
UK publishers can now block their content from appearing in Google's AI search summaries following a ruling by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). The watchdog has required Google to make source attribution more prominent when displaying AI-generated overviews to users.

The CMA said the new requirement puts publishers and news organisations "in a stronger position to negotiate content deals with Google." The ruling addresses publisher concerns about declining click-through traffic and revenue as users get information directly from AI summaries rather than visiting original content.

cards.headline: Possible flesh-eating screwworm infection found in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA reports a possible case of flesh-eating screwworm in South Texas, which would mark the first time the parasite has crossed the US-Mexico border if confirmed.

cards.headline: Meteor that fell in Cape Cod Bay likely made of iron, NASA says
cards.teaser: NASA analysis indicates a meteor that landed in Cape Cod Bay was unusually dense and may have been composed of iron.
cards.body:
A meteor that exploded off the coast of Massachusetts and landed in Cape Cod Bay was likely made of iron and had unusual density, according to NASA. The meteor caused loud booms heard across parts of the United States and Canada when it entered the atmosphere and broke apart.

The space agency provided new details about the size and landing location of the meteor fragments. Reports of the booms came from multiple locations as the meteor streaked through the sky before impacting the water. Iron meteorites are relatively rare compared to rocky ones and tend to survive atmospheric entry better due to their composition.

cards.headline: Uber plans to deploy 500 data-collection vehicles this year
cards.teaser: Uber will put 500 sensor-equipped vehicles on roads in 2026 to gather data for its new autonomous vehicle division.
cards.body:
Uber announced plans to deploy 500 data-collection vehicles on public roads this year. The modified Ioniq 5 electric vehicles will be loaded with sensors designed to capture information for the company's new AV Labs division, which focuses on autonomous vehicle development.

The data-gathering fleet represents a significant expansion of Uber's efforts in the self-driving vehicle space. The sensors on the vehicles will collect road and traffic information that Uber can use to develop and improve autonomous driving systems.

cards.headline: Roblox acquires AI video startup to advance spatial computing push
cards.teaser: Roblox announced the acquisition of Morpheus AI, a video world model lab, as part of its Roblox Reality initiative.
cards.body:
Roblox revealed it has acquired Morpheus, a startup focused on AI-generated video and world models, as part of the company's push into spatial computing called Roblox Reality. The acquisition brings AI founders with expertise in generating three-dimensional content and virtual environments to the gaming platform.

The deal positions Roblox to develop AI-generated machines and creatures that could appear in games on its platform. The company described the technology as enabling part-controllable 3D generation with open vocabulary capabilities, allowing creators to describe and generate custom content using natural language.

cards.headline: Microsoft, Atom Computing, EeroQ provide quantum computing updates
cards.teaser: Several quantum computing companies released progress reports on their technology development efforts.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced a new quantum chip that is 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor. The company expects to develop a quantum computer capable of solving commercially useful problems by the end of the decade.

Quantum computing remains a competitive field, with multiple companies advancing their respective systems. These developments represent progress toward making quantum computers practical tools for real-world applications.

hero.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL after 14 seasons, joins CBS
hero.body:
Russell Wilson announced his retirement from professional football after 14 seasons in the NFL. The quarterback confirmed he will transition to a sports television role with CBS.

Wilson released a video thanking football as he transitions to his new broadcasting career. The announcement marks the end of a career that spanned more than a decade across multiple NFL teams.

Aaron Glenn, commenting on the retirement, congratulated Wilson on his new television position. Glenn indicated his team is evaluating quarterback options following the announcement.

The move to broadcasting represents a common career path for former NFL quarterbacks, who often leverage their on-field experience into media roles. Wilson joins a growing list of recently retired players entering sports television.

Wilson's 14-year career included a Super Bowl championship and multiple Pro Bowl selections. His retirement removes one of the more experienced quarterbacks from the active player pool and creates opportunities for teams seeking veteran leadership at the position.

cards.headline: Rams acquire Myles Garrett in trade from Browns
cards.teaser: The Los Angeles Rams obtained defensive end Myles Garrett in a trade with Cleveland, sending Jared Verse to the Browns.
cards.body:
The Rams completed a blockbuster trade to acquire Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns. The deal sent Jared Verse to Cleveland as part of the exchange between the two teams.

Vikings quarterback Sam Darnold offered limited comment on the Rams acquiring Garrett. Multiple reports described the transaction as a seismic move that could significantly impact league competitive balance.

cards.headline: Arrest warrant issued for 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk
cards.teaser: An arrest warrant was issued for San Francisco 49ers star Brandon Aiyuk in connection with a misdemeanor speeding charge.
cards.body:
Authorities issued an arrest warrant for 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk related to a misdemeanor speeding charge. The warrant stems from an alleged speeding incident near Levis Stadium that was captured on video and circulated online.

The legal development adds uncertainty to Aiyuk's future with the team. The receiver faces potential legal consequences as the case proceeds through the California court system.

cards.headline: Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka loses French Open quarterfinal
cards.teaser: World number one Aryna Sabalenka was defeated by Diana Shnaider in the French Open quarterfinals.
cards.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shocking defeat to 25th seed Diana Shnaider in the French Open quarterfinals, losing 3-6, 7-5, 6-0. The match marked a dramatic collapse, with Sabalenka losing 10 consecutive games during the contest.

In her post-match press conference, Sabalenka expressed her frustration bluntly, saying she wanted "to quit tennis right now." She cited windy conditions as a factor in her performance and suggested the tournament roof should be closed during such weather. Despite her emotional outburst, Sabalenka acknowledged she may feel differently in the coming days.

cards.headline: Padres release outfielder Nick Castellanos after 39 games
cards.teaser: The San Diego Padres designated Nick Castellanos for assignment after a brief stint with the team.
cards.body:
The Padres cut ties with outfielder Nick Castellanos, designating him for assignment after just 39 games with the team. Castellanos returned to Philadelphia during a series against his former team, the Phillies.

Castellanos told reporters he has no regrets about his career decisions. The Padres called up a player named Taylor to fill the roster spot vacated by Castellanos.

cards.headline: Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate reveals battle with depression
cards.teaser: Ibrahima Konate disclosed he battled depression following the deaths of teammate Diogo Jota and his father.
cards.body:
Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate has opened up about battling depression following two significant losses. His former teammate Diogo Jota died, followed by the death of his father, Hamady, in January after a long illness.

The France international's performance on the pitch was affected by the personal turmoil he experienced during this difficult period. Konate spoke publicly about how these tragedies impacted his mental health, highlighting the emotional challenges athletes face beyond their professional duties.

cards.headline: Golden Knights rally to win Stanley Cup Final Game 1
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights came from behind to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes in the opening game of the Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights mounted a comeback to win Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final against the Carolina Hurricanes. The victory gives Vegas an early series lead in the championship round.

The team announced it will host an official watch party at T-Mobile Arena for Game 2 of the series. Game 2 betting lines feature Taylor Hall among recommended wagers for the upcoming matchup.

hero.headline: CBS News Fires Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes
hero.body:
CBS News has terminated Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at 60 Minutes, following a heated confrontation with network leadership over recent staff cuts at the storied program. The firing marks a dramatic moment in ongoing tensions between the show's journalists and CBS News management under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.

The conflict erupted after CBS News fired the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without explaining the reasons for their terminations. During a Monday morning staff meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and other executives, Pelley strongly objected to the changes and directly criticized Weiss's leadership. According to sources, Pelley said that Weiss was "murdering 60 Minutes" and had been "brought in to kill it."

Following the meeting, Weiss and other executives met with Pelley on Tuesday to address his conduct. That evening, Bilton sent Pelley a termination message stating he had been "terminated for cause effective immediately." In the message, Bilton cited Pelley's behavior during the staff meeting, saying Pelley had "hijacked" the meeting "to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Pelley subsequently issued a public statement accusing CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes had maintained its position as the top program in its category because audiences value "integrity, quality, and humanity" in its stories.

The termination has left 60 Minutes with significant staffing challenges. The program now has only three full-time correspondents heading into its 59th season: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and L Jon Wertheim. This follows Anderson Cooper's earlier announcement that he would be leaving the show.

The firings have prompted concern among staff members about editorial independence and the future direction of the news division. Former 60 Minutes correspondent Steve Kroft characterized the changes as "disastrous" and called them "journalistic interference," noting that the program remains the highest rated show in its time slot, which he said makes the management decisions senseless from a business perspective.

Pelley's colleagues have acknowledged his contributions to the network. He joined CBS News in 1989 and served as chief White House correspondent and anchor of the CBS Evening News from 2011 to 2017 before joining 60 Minutes as a correspondent in 1999. His departure reflects broader tensions within media organizations as they balance traditional journalism practices with pressure from various stakeholders.

cards.headline: Steve Kroft Criticizes 60 Minutes Direction Under Bari Weiss
cards.teaser: The 60 Minutes veteran called the program's direction under CBS News boss Bari Weiss disastrous and labeled it journalistic interference.
cards.body:
Steve Kroft, a former 60 Minutes correspondent, criticized the current direction of the program under CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, calling the situation "disastrous" and characterizing it as journalistic interference. Kroft made these comments during an interview with PBS NewsHour reporter Geoff Bennett.

His remarks came after CBS News fired Scott Pelley, the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. Pelley had confronted leadership at a staff meeting, accusing them of "murdering" the news program. Kroft noted that 60 Minutes remains the highest-rated program in its category, suggesting the changes made no business sense.

cards.headline: Matt Brown Found Dead at 42
cards.teaser: The Alaskan Bush People star's body was found in a Washington state river, with his brother Noah helping to recover it.
cards.body:
Matt Brown, a star of the reality television series Alaskan Bush People, has died at age 42. His body was found in a river in Washington state, with his brother Noah among those who helped pull the body from the water.

Brown's stepsister later described what she characterized as a self-serving feeling surrounding some of the tributes that followed his death. The cause of death has been confirmed by authorities, though specific details about the circumstances surrounding his death have been released.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Addresses Past Comments About Playing Spider-Man in His 30s
cards.teaser: The actor, now 30, revealed his 2021 statement about not playing the character past that age may have been a negotiating strategy.
cards.body:
In 2021, Tom Holland told GQ magazine that playing Spider-Man past age 30 would indicate he'd made a mistake. Now that he's reached 30 and has a new Spider-Man film, Brand New Day, arriving in theaters on July 31, Holland is reframing those earlier remarks.

Holland suggested his 2021 comments may have been a negotiating tactic with Sony. He described the statement as "a strategy to create fear," implying he was attempting to leverage the studio for better contract terms. He currently has no plans to retire from the role.

cards.headline: TikTok Launches Microseries Writing Workshop with Sundance Institute
cards.teaser: The four-week program aims to support creators developing short-form scripted content for digital platforms.
cards.body:
TikTok and Sundance Institute have partnered to launch a microseries writing program through Sundance Collab, the institute's digital learning platform. The collaboration aims to cultivate the next generation of creator-led short-form storytelling on digital platforms.

The four-week online course teaches creators how to write and produce microdramas and other scripted short-form series designed specifically for digital audiences. Through this program, participants will develop essential skills needed to create compelling content within TikTok's format constraints.

cards.headline: Lena the Plug Files for Divorce from Adam22
cards.teaser: The OnlyFans model is seeking custody of the couple's five-year-old daughter and receives $3,000 in monthly spousal support.
cards.body:
Lena the Plug has filed for divorce from Adam22, according to court documents. The OnlyFans model is seeking custody of their five-year-old daughter as part of the divorce proceedings.

Court documents show Lena the Plug receives $3,000 in monthly spousal support. Following news of the split, Adam22, a podcaster, publicly asked for Black women to direct message him.

cards.headline: Variety Holds Inaugural Power of Women London Event
cards.teaser: Cynthia Erivo, Emilia Clarke, Suki Waterhouse, Emma Corrin and Hannah Waddingham were honored at the event, with a surprise appearance from Joan Collins.
cards.body:
Variety held its first Power of Women London event at the Chancery Rosewood Hotel, presented by Lifetime. The gathering honored Cynthia Erivo, Emilia Clarke, Suki Waterhouse, Emma Corrin and Hannah Waddingham, with the five women reflecting on their careers, community importance and charitable causes.

The event, hosted by Saturday Night Live U.K., featured a surprise appearance from Dame Joan Collins. The honorees discussed the need to reinvent themselves throughout their careers and the work they support through various organizations.

hero.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to full ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
hero.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire, according to a joint statement released by the United States, Israel, and Lebanon following U.S.-mediated talks at the State Department in Washington DC. The agreement requires Hezbollah to halt attacks completely and evacuate all its operatives from areas south of the Litani River.

The joint statement emphasized that both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The statement also called for the Lebanese army to take full control of security zones that would be established within Lebanon, though specifics on how these zones would be created remain unclear.

The ceasefire represents the latest attempt to stabilize a volatile situation. Israel and Lebanon previously agreed to a truce last month, but fighting has continued since that announcement. Israeli strikes have killed more than 800 people in Lebanon following the earlier agreement, while Hezbollah has continued targeting Israeli troops in southern Lebanon and launching rockets toward northern Israel.

Recent military escalation has been severe. Israel has attacked three hospitals in southern Lebanon within one week, killing nine people and wounding more than 150 according to Lebanon's health ministry. Israeli troops have also advanced deeper into southern Lebanon than they have in approximately 25 years, raising their flag over the ancient Beaufort Castle over the weekend. In response, Hezbollah launched deeper rocket attacks into northern Israel.

A significant challenge to implementation remains uncertain. Hezbollah, which operates as a semi-autonomous armed force within Lebanon, is not directly participating in the negotiations and has firmly rejected the talks. The organization has stated it will not comply with any agreements resulting from the Israel-Lebanon discussions. While the Lebanese government has accepted the ceasefire terms, Hezbollah's willingness to accept the withdrawal requirement south of the Litani River is unclear.

The two sides agreed to reconvene for additional talks beginning June 22 to work toward a comprehensive peace and security agreement. The timing reflects the fragile nature of the current arrangement.

The agreement comes as the U.S. pursues broader diplomatic efforts in the Middle East. President Trump has indicated he wants to keep Lebanon separate from Iran peace negotiations, describing them as "a very different kind of thing." Iranian officials have warned that any attack on Beirut would trigger a wider resumption of conflict in the Middle East.

The conditional nature of the ceasefire leaves open the possibility that fighting could resume if Hezbollah rejects the terms or if either side fails to implement them as outlined. Implementation success will likely determine whether this agreement achieves lasting stability or becomes another temporary pause in the conflict.

cards.headline: House passes Iran war powers resolution with bipartisan support
cards.teaser: Several Republicans joined Democrats to pass a resolution forcing the Trump administration to end its war against Iran.
cards.body:
The House voted 215-208 to pass a war powers resolution requiring the Trump administration to seek congressional approval before continuing hostilities with Iran or withdraw U.S. forces. Four Republicans crossed party lines to support the measure: Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan.

The resolution represents a rare bipartisan rebuke of the administration's Iran policy. However, the measure faces significant obstacles to becoming law. Democrats have struggled to advance similar legislation in the Senate, and the measure would likely face a presidential veto even if passed there.

cards.headline: House floor debate erupts over Lebanon war powers resolution
cards.teaser: Representative Rashida Tlaib's push for a Lebanon war powers resolution sparked cross-partisan conflict that briefly halted House proceedings.
cards.body:
Tensions in the House escalated Wednesday as both Democrats and Republicans criticized Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan over her efforts to pass a Lebanon war powers resolution. The dispute briefly ground the chamber to a halt during floor debate.

Representative Max Miller, an Ohio Republican, said during debate on the measure that Hezbollah is a terrorist organization and its members are butchers that Tlaib likes to hang out with to a certain extent. The fight had already divided Democrats before sparking the cross-partisan exchange.

cards.headline: Trump to announce $700 million in coal industry funding
cards.teaser: The administration plans to use wartime authority to direct hundreds of millions of dollars to existing coal plants and export infrastructure.
cards.body:
President Trump is expected to announce that his administration will allocate approximately $700 million to bolster the coal industry. The funding will be distributed using wartime authority under the Defense Production Act.

The announcement includes $425 million for 13 existing coal plants and $75 million for an export terminal in California. An additional $185 million is expected to be announced for unspecified purposes related to coal production and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Iran war could cause prolonged energy disruption and global recession
cards.teaser: A new economic outlook warns that extended energy supply disruptions from the Iran conflict would severely damage the global economy.
cards.body:
The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development warned that sustained energy supply disruptions from the Iran conflict would severely damage the global economy, potentially triggering recessions and job losses across multiple countries.

The conflict's ripple effects are already visible. Japan is experiencing shortages of plastic bags, trays, and food service gloves as naphtha—a key plastic ingredient extracted from crude oil—becomes scarce. The Middle East supplies most of Japan's crude oil, and the food sector alone accounts for nearly one-third of the country's annual plastic consumption. Some Japanese retailers are now offering incentives to customers who bring their own containers.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, a former Biden administration official, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico and will advance to the general election.

If Haaland wins in November, she would become the first female Native American governor in the United States.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early results in the California primary show competitive races between multiple Democrats and Republicans vying to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
With nearly 60% of votes counted, Republican Steve Hilton held a narrow lead in California's gubernatorial primary, followed by Democrat Xavier Becerra in second place. Tom Steyer, a billionaire environmental activist running as a progressive Democrat, trailed in third.

The state's vote-counting process was progressing slowly, with officials indicating the full results could take days or even weeks to finalize. California's top-two primary system places all candidates on a single ballot regardless of party affiliation, with the top two vote-getters advancing to the general election to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
